correctness.rationale: The all-positive trace forces each nontrivial component into one triple; a cycle cannot realize a trace with just one negative cycle edge. Thus the components are paths on three vertices and single edges, and each needs its own triple. In the two excluded saturated profiles one can force m−1 full path triples, leaving the selected query forced positive in the last triple. For sufficiency, consider the Hall condition on vacant slots: slots in two distinct boxes jointly admit every mover, and slots in one nonfree box with t vacancies need t movers originating outside it. A spare free box supplies three movers, and in the saturated case the q≥2 single-edge boxes each supply one, enough for any two-leaf path box and for every single-edge box. Staying at the fixed endpoint versus moving to a different box realizes each required sign without affecting positive queries. Counting labelled components gives the stated factorial expression; the two top-degree profiles for m≥2 give the top coefficient, and m=1 leaves only the empty support. An independent partition-trace census of all 8 and 32,768 supports for m=1 and m=2 agreed (coefficients 1 and 1,15,105).
residual_risks: The independent census is bounded at m≤2; the unrestricted statement rests on the combinatorial proof, not finite testing or formal verification.

value.rationale: A complete support classification for a natural constrained equivalence class distinguishes actual shattering from mere feasibility of the all-positive trace. The explicit saturation obstructions and completion proof add content beyond a dimension estimate; the exact census then reports how often each support size occurs.
residual_risks: This resolves the triple-block family only, not general size-constrained partitions or adaptive query complexity.
